clean_methods: group consecutive tokens into semantic chunks of size c - This establishes the semantic unit that ChunkKV preserves instead of individual tokens, directly supporting the hypothesis that chunks maintain contextual relationships.

Calculate observation scores for chunks by summing attention scores across tokens within each chunk - This provides the chunk-level importance signal used to decide which semantic units remain in the KV cache.

Select the top-k chunks based on these aggregated scores using the same selection policy as existing methods - This operationalizes compression by retaining the highest-scoring semantic chunks under a fixed cache budget.

Preserve the sequential order of selected chunks to maintain narrative flow - This keeps the temporal and narrative structure of the context, which is important for long-context reasoning and multi-document QA.
Concatenate an observation window to retain recent important information - This ensures recent tokens remain available, complementing chunk selection with recency-sensitive context.

computing chunk selection only for every Nth layer and reusing those indices for intermediate layers - This implements layer-wise index reuse, reducing repeated chunk-selection overhead by exploiting similar preserved indices across adjacent layers.

implement ChunkKV as a drop-in replacement for existing KV cache compression methods - This makes the semantic chunking approach deployable within current transformer inference stacks without architectural changes.

evaluate ChunkKV on LongBench and Needle-In-A-Haystack (NIAH) benchmarks using LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2-7B-Instruct models - This tests whether semantic chunk preservation improves long-context QA, retrieval, and multi-document comprehension across representative LLMs.

evaluate across 17 datasets covering single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, and synthetic tasks - This broadens LongBench coverage to test semantic preservation across diverse long-context task types.
test retrieval capabilities across context lengths of 8k and 32k tokens - This probes whether ChunkKV can locate and use relevant information in increasingly long contexts.

test compression ratios of 10%, 20%, and 30% to assess performance across different memory constraints - This measures how ChunkKV trades accuracy against cache size under increasingly aggressive compression.

compare ChunkKV against existing methods (StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV) using identical experimental settings - This isolates the contribution of semantic chunk preservation by benchmarking against established token-level or alternative KV compression baselines.

measure both task performance and computational efficiency, including compression time and memory usage - This evaluates whether semantic preservation improves accuracy without sacrificing the efficiency gains that motivate KV cache compression.

conduct systematic ablation studies to determine optimal chunk sizes ranging from 1 to 30 tokens, evaluate the effectiveness of layer-wise index reuse across different numbers of reuse layers, and analyze the trade-offs between compression efficiency and performance degradation - This identifies the design choices that drive ChunkKV's accuracy-efficiency behavior.

quantify the semantic preservation capabilities of ChunkKV by measuring layer-wise similarity of preserved indices using Jaccard similarity coefficients and analyzing attention pattern preservation compared to discrete token methods - This provides direct evidence that chunk-based compression retains more coherent attention structure than token-level compression.

assess ChunkKV's effectiveness on GSM8K arithmetic reasoning tasks with Chain-of-Thought prompting at a 30% compression ratio - This tests whether semantic chunk preservation helps maintain multi-step reasoning chains in in-context learning settings.

evaluate performance across multiple languages using Qwen2-7B-Instruct on Chinese subtasks to assess cross-lingual effectiveness - This checks whether the semantic chunking strategy generalizes beyond English-centric long-context tasks.

All experiments will be conducted three times with mean scores reported to ensure statistical robustness - This reduces variance in benchmark results and supports reliable comparison across methods and settings.
